metadata.note: The L&N/Seaboard Gulf Wind along the Gulf Coast, the historical predecessor of Amtrak's Mardi Gras Service between New Orleans and Mobile. Route geometry is taken from the modern Amtrak route's own GTFS-sourced alignment for this corridor (see amtrak.geojson), since the historical train ran the same physical line; where the historical train ran beyond or differently from today's Amtrak route, that is described in the segment notes. Era boundaries follow real, sourced milestones; headway_min and avg_speed_kmh within each era are estimates, not from real timetables.
metadata.line_label_audit: 2026-08-24: line labels normalised repo-wide to "<operating company>: <line name>" -- the company's common display name (legal suffixes dropped), then the line as a passenger would have known it, or its two terminals where the line carried no advertised name. Long intermediate station lists were reduced to endpoints. For features spanning several operators the company shown is the one that ran the line for most of its drawn years. See CLAUDE.md Rule 6.

segments.note: The Gulf Wind was inaugurated Jul 31 1949 as a joint L&N/Seaboard Air Line streamliner hugging the Gulf Coast between New Orleans and Jacksonville - L&N rails as far as Chattahoochee, Seaboard beyond. Its consist typically ran two coaches, two sleepers, and separate L&N and Seaboard diners, including L&N's only round-end observation cars. (This geometry shows the New Orleans-Mobile portion Amtrak's Mardi Gras Service revived in 2025; the Gulf Wind continued east to Jacksonville.) It and the South Wind were the last L&N passenger trains in Florida, running until Amtrak took over May 1 1971 - see amtrak.geojson. estimated; frequency not sourced from a real timetable
